result.question: Survey UI options and the community tools/plugins ecosystem for the pi coding agent (earendil-works/pi, npm @earendil-works/*, ~100k stars) as of September 2026. Given: pi has no first-party GUI; surfaces are TUI, print/JSON, RPC mode (pi --mode rpc), and a TypeScript SDK (AgentSession); pi-web-ui is a first-party web-chat component library lagging core; sessions are JSONL trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/; pi packages install via npm:/git: with a gallery at pi.dev/packages; earendil-works/pi-chat is separate Slack automation; ruizrica/agent-pi and Dwsy/pi-session-manager exist. GOAL 1 — census and assess community/third-party UIs (web, desktop, IDE, remote/mobile, session viewers, TUI layers): attachment mechanism (RPC/SDK/pi-web-ui/JSONL), maturity, macOS + native Windows viability, provider-agnosticism, current vs stale @mariozechner scope; plus whether pi-web-ui caught up/became an app and any official UI roadmap. GOAL 2 — census the pi package ecosystem (extensions, skills, themes, awesome-pi lists, hubs) distinguishing adopt-now from study-for-patterns and flagging single-maintainer/no-CI/stale-scope/security risks. End with a ranked UI shortlist and a tools/plugins shortlist, noting where building on RPC/SDK beats adopting. Prioritize primary sources.

results.title: Issue #563 — feat(coding-agent): Add MCP extension example (earendil-works/pi)
results.snippet: THE canonical MCP-bridge lineage the question calls out. Opened by badlogic (core maintainer) 2026-01-08, now CLOSED. Design: pi ships NO built-in MCP; an extension reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and <cwd>/.pi/mcp.json (Claude Code-compatible format), connects over stdio + SSE via the MCP TypeScript SDK, exposes server tools as mcp_<server>_<tool>, and adds a /mcp UI (server list with green/red status, per-server enable/disable via setActiveTools). This is the adopt-or-clone reference pattern for wiring your own MCP into pi via the extension API rather than waiting for first-party support.

results.title: Pi Packages — official docs (security model for packages/extensions/skills)
results.snippet: Primary source for the security lens. States plainly that pi packages run with FULL SYSTEM ACCESS: extensions execute arbitrary code and skills can instruct the model to run any executable, so you must review source before installing third-party packages. Confirms install mechanics (pi install npm:@foo/pi-tools / git:github.com/…), pi-package keyword for gallery discovery, and that skills load on-demand for progressive disclosure without busting the prompt cache. This is the risk baseline every third-party extension/UI inherits.

results.title: pi coding-agent extensions.md — extension system + capability/security surface
results.snippet: Authoritative capability map: extensions are TypeScript modules that register custom tools, add slash commands, intercept events, modify the system prompt, and register a complete Provider (composition base, with models.json overrides still applying above it) — the mechanism behind provider extensions and sub-agents. Critically, pi has NO built-in permission system for filesystem/process/network/credential access and runs with user permissions by default; stronger boundaries require external containerization/sandboxing. Establishes that a 'sandbox extension' cannot truly confine — real isolation is an OS-level concern, not an in-process extension.

results.title: ruizrica/agent-pi — multi-agent orchestration extension suite (maturity/risk profile)
results.snippet: Best study-for-patterns candidate AND the clearest single-maintainer flag. ~267 stars / 41 forks, MIT, ~60 commits, one maintainer (Ricardo Ruiz), NO visible CI, no release/version history — operational risk for adopt-now. 43 extensions incl. orchestration (team/chain/pipeline + subagent widgets), an optional 'commander-mcp' bridge, a pre-execution guard + project-sweep + message-integrity 'security' cluster, and browser-based plan-approval/report/spec viewers (relevant to the UI question). Builds ON pi via the extension API (no fork); Node/TS so nominally cross-platform but macOS/Windows testing is undocumented. Mine it for patterns; don't take a hard dependency.

results.title: CaptCanadaMan/pi-ollama — native Ollama provider extension (fixes tool-calling under streaming)
results.snippet: Concrete example of the Provider-registration extension pattern and its failure modes. Registers a native 'ollama' provider with a custom streamSimple handler; specifically detects the generated≫streamed token gap where Ollama silently drops tool calls under streaming and raises a RETRYABLE error instead of completing silently. Illustrates why provider-agnosticism at the pi layer still needs per-provider extension glue — and carries the usual single-maintainer/community-provider risk versus first-party support.

results.title: Issue #4155 — Official local-LLM provider extensions (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, Ollama)

result.summary: As of September 2026 pi still ships no first-party GUI: first-party interface investment in the current release window went into the TUI (v0.84.0 "Fullscreen TUI mode" plus follow-on search/scroll/selection work), and the first-party @earendil-works/pi-web-ui remains a reusable component LIBRARY frozen at 0.75.3 (~mid-May 2026), well behind an actively-released core at 0.84.4 — it has neither caught up nor been promoted to a shippable app. The community has nonetheless produced a real spread of third-party UIs, all attaching through the two officially-sanctioned surfaces: RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`, strict-JSONL over stdio, documented for embedding in apps/IDEs/custom UIs, live and maintained with a shipped RpcClient) and the TypeScript SDK (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent AgentSession — the docs-preferred path for JS/TS builders, listing "build a custom UI (web, desktop, mobile)" as an intended use case). The strongest candidate for our needs is BlackBeltTechnology/pi-agent-dashboard, a maintained Electron+web multi-session controller with native Windows x64/ARM64 installers (the only project with proven native-Windows viability), though it attaches via a bespoke in-pi Bridge Extension + dual WebSocket gateways and targets the stale @mariozechner scope. Credible alternatives include samfoy/pi-dashboard (web + native iOS, RPC-mode, alpha), preinpost/pi-web-chat and xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui (SDK+WebSocket web apps on the current scope), and svkozak/pi-acp for Zed IDE embedding. Note: the tools/plugins census the research goals asked for (gallery popularity, git/sandboxing/sub-agent/MCP-bridge/provider extensions, skills, themes, awesome-pi lists) is essentially absent from the verified claims and remains an open gap.

findings.claim: Official attachment surfaces are RPC mode and the TypeScript SDK. RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`) is officially documented as the mechanism for embedding the agent in other applications, IDEs, or custom UIs; the SDK (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, current scope) lists 'Build a custom UI (web, desktop, mobile)' as an intended use case. The RPC docs explicitly steer Node.js/TypeScript builders to use AgentSession directly rather than spawning the RPC subprocess — so within JS/TS the SDK is the preferred path, while RPC serves other-language/IDE embedders.
findings.evidence: rpc.md verbatim: RPC mode is 'useful for embedding the agent in other applications, IDEs, or custom UIs' and 'If you're building a Node.js application, consider using AgentSession directly from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent instead of spawning a subprocess.' sdk.md lists 'Build a custom UI (web, desktop, mobile)' as the leading example use case; npm confirms name @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, latest 0.84.4, ships bin.pi + SDK type exports, current @earendil-works scope (not stale @mariozechner). All four component claims 3-0.

findings.claim: RPC mode is a live, maintained embedding surface, not dormant: it ships a client library (RpcClient in packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/), is under active development (v0.84.4 Aug 28 added `clear_queue` RPC queue clearing; v0.82.0 Jul 24 added session-aware streaming bash_execution_update events for direct RPC), and is under active bug-fixing (RpcClient issue #8965 opened Sep 1 2026). Any custom UI client embedding via RPC must implement a strict-JSONL framing constraint: LF (\n) is the only record delimiter and generic line readers (e.g. Node's readline) are non-compliant because they also split on U+2028/U+2029, which are valid inside JSON strings.
findings.evidence: rpc.md verbatim: 'RPC mode uses strict JSONL semantics with LF (\n) as the only record delimiter' and warns Node readline 'is not protocol-compliant... it also splits on U+2028 and U+2029'. Release notes confirm v0.84.4 RPC queue clearing and v0.82.0 streaming bash RPC events. Issue #8965 (RpcClient.waitForIdle) opened Sep 1 2026 confirms active maintenance. Caveat (from a 2-1 vote): #8965 is 'closed as not planned' and Sep 1 is its opened date, so it is not a same-day fix — but the maintained-surface conclusion holds on independent evidence (#4764, #3275).

findings.claim: BlackBeltTechnology/pi-agent-dashboard is the strongest Windows-viable UI candidate: an Electron desktop app plus React/Tailwind/Vite web dashboard for real-time monitoring and control of multiple parallel pi sessions (spawn, watch reasoning live, force-kill, mobile/remote via mDNS or zrok), shipping native Windows x64 AND ARM64 installers (v0.8.0, Aug 26 2026), macOS .dmg and Linux packages — 267 stars, near-monthly cadence, real-org maintained. It does NOT attach via RPC mode or raw JSONL; it uses an in-pi Bridge Extension (auto-started, forwards events, relays commands, hosts PromptBus) over dual WebSocket gateways (Pi Gateway :9999, Browser Gateway :8000). Two adoption flags: Windows binaries are unsigned (SmartScreen bypass), and it targets the STALE @mariozechner scope.
findings.evidence: GitHub API confirms v0.8.0 (2026-08-26) with native Windows installers PI-Dashboard-Setup-0.8.0-x64.exe and -arm64.exe plus portable zips, macOS .dmg, Linux .AppImage/.deb; stack React+Tailwind+Vite/Fastify/Electron/xterm.js+node-pty. architecture.md (second primary doc) confirms Bridge Extension auto-registers/auto-starts and dual gateways on exact ports :9999/:8000. Nuance (2-1 on the mechanism claim): historical sessions ARE loaded from disk via SessionManager (pi SDK), only the live mirror goes through the bridge, so 'never reads JSONL' is slightly overstated. node-pty ARM64 may need VS Build Tools in edge cases. Targets @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent, not @earendil-works.
findings.vote: 3-0 on existence/Windows/features (claim 0); 2-1 on the bridge-extension mechanism detail (claim 1)

findings.claim: samfoy/pi-dashboard is a community web + native iOS dashboard (chat with pi, manage multiple sessions, browse files, run terminals from browser or iPhone). It attaches via RPC mode: the backend spawns one `pi --mode rpc` process per chat slot, tracks slot state in ~/.pi/agent/pi-web-sessions.json, and reads message history from pi's session JSONL files on demand. The iOS app is a genuine SwiftUI Xcode project (not aspirational). Flags: alpha status, single maintainer, and the README links the stale @mariozechner scope.
findings.evidence: README verbatim tagline matches the claim; backend spawns pi as a child process in JSON-RPC mode, one per chat slot, persists slot metadata to ~/.pi/agent/pi-web-sessions.json, loads history from session files on demand. apple/PiDash/ contains a real PiDash.xcodeproj (SwiftUI, PiDashShare/PiDashWidget/PiDashTests). 49 stars, MIT, created 2026-04-14, pushed 2026-07-22 (current). README references the stale mariozechner scope; badge is 'alpha'. Both claims 3-0.

findings.claim: preinpost/pi-web-chat is a third-party, single-maintainer standalone web UI, self-described as OpenWebUI-style and mobile-friendly (safe-area/dvh layout), on the CURRENT @earendil-works scope. It attaches via the pi SDK (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) plus a WebSocket server, installed as a pi package EXTENSION (`pi install npm:pi-web-chat`) that registers `/web` (slash command) and `pi --web` (CLI) to launch a Node web-server daemon on localhost:3141 — not RPC mode, not pi-web-ui components, not raw JSONL reading. Latest 0.1.19, Aug 11 2026 (current). MIT, ~3 stars.
findings.evidence: npm registry: description 'Web UI for the pi coding agent (OpenWebUI-style, mobile-friendly)', author minsoo.lee/preinpost, MIT, latest 0.1.19 (2026-08-11), single maintainer. pi.dev gallery: 'Server: Node with @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK and WebSocket (ws)'; extension type; registers pi --web + /web; 'pi --web starts only the web server daemon and exits'; default port 3141. Standalone-CLI mode confirmed. Negative (no RPC/no pi-web-ui/no JSONL) is a sound inference from confirmed architecture. Both claims 3-0.

findings.claim: The unscoped npm package `pi-web-ui` (github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui, sole maintainer xingshuyin) is a DISTINCT third-party artifact from the first-party @earendil-works/pi-web-ui component library — it is a full, deployable web-chat application (one-command run; Docker/systemd/launchd deployable; built-in terminal, git, file management). It attaches by running the pi SDK inside a server-side process and streaming events to the browser over WebSocket (ws), and it depends on the CURRENT @earendil-works scope, pinning @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ^0.84.4 — matching current core, not the stale @mariozechner scope. MIT, latest 0.59.0.
findings.evidence: npm registry: unscoped name pi-web-ui, description 'Web chat interface for the pi coding agent, powered by the pi SDK (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) — one-command run, Docker/systemd/launchd deployable', sole maintainer xingshuyin, repo github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui, MIT, latest 0.59.0; dependencies include @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ^0.84.4 + ws ^8.18.0 + express + node-pty, no @mariozechner dep. Distinct from first-party scoped @earendil-works/pi-web-ui. NOTE: a separate claim that this app 'supports native Windows' (Git Bash terminal auto-select, Windows Scheduled Task deploy) was REFUTED 1-2, so its native-Windows viability is unproven. Both surviving claims 3-0.

findings.claim: The first-party @earendil-works/pi-web-ui is a reusable web-chat COMPONENT LIBRARY (powered by @earendil-works/pi-ai + @earendil-works/pi-agent-core), NOT a standalone app, and has not been promoted to a shippable application. It attaches to the agent via the SDK (an in-process Agent instance passed through setAgent() with optional callbacks; uses IndexedDB browser storage) — not RPC mode or session-JSONL reading. Its latest version is 0.75.3, published ~mid-May 2026 (2026-05-18; last-modified 2026-05-27); it remains well behind actively-released core (0.84.4, 2026-08-28) and has NOT caught up or been re-released since May.
findings.evidence: npm registry (queried 2026-09-01): @earendil-works/pi-web-ui dist-tags.latest=0.75.3 (published 2026-05-18), no bin field/no executable entry (library not app), description 'Reusable web UI components for AI chat interfaces'; no version >=0.76 exists. Attachment via ChatPanel.setAgent(agent, {...}); README states integration is 'declarative and state-based rather than using RPC or JSONL file reading'. Core (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/pi-agent-core/pi-tui) all at 0.84.4 (2026-08-28), confirming the gap. Disambiguation: the deployable 'pi-web-ui' app is the unscoped third-party package, a separate namesake. All three claims 3-0.

findings.claim: svkozak/pi-acp is a community ACP (Agent Client Protocol) adapter giving pi an IDE-embedding surface without pi shipping first-party IDE integration: it spawns `pi --mode rpc` and bridges ACP JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio to an ACP client. Its primary (effectively only well-supported) client is the Zed editor — other ACP clients have varying/untested compatibility, so it is not a general cross-editor solution today. ~656 stars, actively maintained (self-described MVP-style, expect minor breaking changes). Sibling ACP adapters exist (aksdb/pi-acp-bridge, 0xSero/pi-acp, nyanshak/pi-extensions) plus official discussion #4444.
findings.evidence: README verbatim: 'communicates ACP JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio to an ACP client (e.g. Zed editor) and spawns pi --mode rpc, bridging requests/events' and purpose is IDE integration 'without requiring modifications to the core pi codebase'; 'Development is centered around Zed editor support' and 'other clients may have varying levels of compatibility'. Only Zed gets named/tested features (startup info blocks, session history v0.225.0+, Authenticate banner). Corroborated by DeepWiki + npm; complementary svkozak/pi-acp-zed extension reinforces Zed focus. 144 commits, 656 stars. Both claims 3-0.

findings.claim: Zetaphor/pi-vscode-extension attaches to pi via the TypeScript SDK, embedding the agent as a bundled npm dependency (PiSessionManager wraps createAgentSession) rather than via RPC mode, pi-web-ui components, or session-JSONL reading — so pi need not be installed separately. However, it targets the STALE @mariozechner npm scope (depends on @mariozechner/pi-agent-core and @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent pinned ^0.70.2, predating the 0.74.0 migration to @earendil-works) — a concrete stale-scope adoption risk for anyone standardizing on current pi. Other pi VS Code extensions exist (pithings/pi-vscode, marketplace pi0.pi-vscode, johnny-zhao.pi-agent-studio).
findings.evidence: README: 'This extension embeds the Pi coding agent SDK as an npm dependency' and 'You do not need to install Pi separately'; PiSessionManager 'wraps createAgentSession from @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent' (in-process SDK, not RPC-over-stdio); no mention of RPC/JSONL/pi-web-ui. package.json depends on @mariozechner/pi-agent-core ^0.70.2 and @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent ^0.70.2 (no @earendil-works dep). Migration to @earendil-works began at v0.74.0 (current core 0.84.4), so the ^0.70.2 pin is literally pre-migration and deprecated. Both claims 3-0.

findings.claim: First-party interface investment in the current release window went into the TUI, not a GUI/web app. v0.84.0 (Aug 6 2026) introduced 'Fullscreen TUI mode' (sticky editor/footer, independently scrollable transcript, draggable scrollbars, Mermaid/LaTeX rendering), followed by v0.84.1 word/paragraph selection + half-page scrolling, v0.84.2 fullscreen transcript search (Ctrl+Shift+F), and v0.84.4 fullscreen selection copy controls. No web-UI/GUI/web-app release appears in the v0.81.0–v0.84.4 window.
findings.evidence: GitHub releases + official Pi Changelog + pi.dev/news confirm v0.84.0 Fullscreen TUI mode verbatim and the follow-on TUI features across v0.84.1/.2/.4. WebFetch of the full v0.81.0–v0.84.4 list found no GUI/web-app release; first-party pi-web-ui component library last shipped 2026-05-27 (before this window). 'Not a GUI/web app' is a mild absence-based inference but well-grounded. NOTE: a stronger claim that release notes mention NO embedding/custom-UI roadmap at all was REFUTED 1-2 (RPC additions do appear), so this finding is scoped to interface-surface investment, not roadmap silence. Claim 20 was 3-0.

findings.claim: SYNTHESIS — Ranked UI shortlist. ADOPT/pilot: (1) BlackBeltTechnology/pi-agent-dashboard — Electron+web multi-session controller, the ONLY candidate with proven native Windows x64/ARM64 installers; attaches via bespoke Bridge Extension + dual WebSockets; flags = unsigned Windows binaries, stale @mariozechner scope. STUDY-THEN-BUILD (all Node-server web UIs, POSIX-assumed, native-Windows unverified): (2) preinpost/pi-web-chat — SDK+ws, current scope, mobile-friendly, but ~3 stars/single maintainer; (3) xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui — SDK+ws deployable app, current scope ^0.84.4, single maintainer; (4) samfoy/pi-dashboard — web+native iOS, RPC-mode, alpha/single maintainer, stale scope. IDE lane: (5) svkozak/pi-acp — Zed-only today; (6) Zetaphor/pi-vscode-extension — SDK-embedded but AVOID for current-scope work (pinned stale ^0.70.2). Given every third-party option is single-maintainer/alpha or stale-scoped, building our own on the SDK (AgentSession, docs-preferred for TS) or RPC beats adopting for anything load-bearing — study these for attachment patterns rather than depend on them.
findings.evidence: The per-project facts (attachment mechanism, maturity, scope, Windows viability) are each high-confidence and primary-sourced above; the RANKING is editorial synthesis judgment, hence medium. Native-Windows viability is verified ONLY for pi-agent-dashboard (installers per GitHub API); for the Node-server web UIs it is unproven (the one explicit native-Windows support claim, for xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui, was REFUTED 1-2). The 'build-our-own beats adopt' recommendation follows from the sanctioned-surface findings (SDK/RPC are first-party, documented, maintained) combined with the single-maintainer/alpha/stale-scope risk profile of every adoptable candidate.
findings.vote: synthesis (derived from claims 0-3, 9-19; ranking is editorial)

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity: all versions/dates are pinned to ~Sept 1 2026 (core @earendil-works 0.84.4, pi-agent-dashboard v0.8.0 Aug 26, first-party pi-web-ui frozen 0.75.3 since ~May); the ecosystem moves fast and these will drift. Native-Windows viability is PROVEN only for BlackBeltTechnology/pi-agent-dashboard (signed-off by actual x64/ARM64 installers, though unsigned → SmartScreen; node-pty ARM64 may need VS Build Tools); for every other web UI (pi-web-chat, xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui, samfoy/pi-dashboard) native-Windows support is UNVERIFIED — they are Node servers so likely portable, but the one explicit native-Windows claim (xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui Git Bash terminal + Scheduled Task) was REFUTED (1-2), so treat POSIX/Git-Bash assumptions as the risk. Scope risk: pi-agent-dashboard, samfoy/pi-dashboard, and Zetaphor/pi-vscode-extension target the STALE @mariozechner scope (Zetaphor pinned pre-migration ^0.70.2); pi-web-chat and xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui are on the current @earendil-works scope. Maintainer risk: nearly every third-party UI is single-maintainer and/or alpha (samfoy alpha; xing-shuyin, preinpost, Zetaphor solo). Two supporting claims rested on 2-1 votes: the pi-agent-dashboard 'never reads JSONL' mechanism detail (overstated — historical sessions load from disk via SDK) and the RpcClient issue #8965 status (it is closed-as-not-planned, and Sep 1 is its opened date, not a same-day fix). BIGGEST GAP: the tools/plugins census the research goals explicitly requested — pi.dev/packages gallery popularity, notable extensions (git workflow, sandboxing, sub-agents, plan mode, MCP bridges from issue #563 lineage, provider extensions like pi-ollama-provider), skills collections, themes, awesome-pi curated lists, and security posture of packages (which run with full system access) — is essentially UNCOVERED by the verified claims; only incidental mentions (BubblePtr/awesome-pi, ruizrica/agent-pi from context) surfaced. CI/no-CI status and security review were not examined for any candidate.
openQuestions: What is actually popular and notable in the pi.dev/packages gallery? The tools/plugins census (git/sandboxing/sub-agent/plan-mode extensions, MCP bridges, provider extensions like pi-ollama-provider, skills collections, themes, awesome-pi lists) went unverified and needs a dedicated primary-source pass, including the full-system-access security posture of packages.

Do the Node-server web UIs (preinpost/pi-web-chat, xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui, samfoy/pi-dashboard) actually run on native Windows (PowerShell/cmd + node-pty), or do they assume POSIX/Git Bash? Only pi-agent-dashboard has proven native-Windows viability.

Does earendil-works have any explicit first-party GUI/web-app roadmap in issues/discussions/announcements, or is TUI-plus-embedding-surfaces (RPC/SDK) the deliberate long-term stance? (The 'no roadmap mention' claim was refuted, so this is genuinely open.)
